create.name: E-Vam Institute
create.bio:
E-Vam Institute is a Tibetan Buddhist centre on Lygon Street in Princes Hill, in Melbourne's inner north, founded in 1982 by Traleg Kyabgon Rinpoche IX. Rinpoche, born in eastern Tibet in 1955 and enthroned as a small child as supreme abbot of Thrangu Monastery, trained in exile at Rumtek and Sarnath and came to Australia in 1980, where he taught for some thirty years until his death in 2012. The institute keeps his approach alive, with study, contemplation and practice rooted mainly in the Kagyu and Nyingma schools of Tibetan Buddhism, alongside courses that look at other traditions. Its sister property, Maitripa Centre, is a retreat place in the mountain ash forest outside Healesville.

Much of the programme draws on recordings of Rinpoche's own teachings. A quarterly Meditation and Teachings series gives full days of meditation, recorded talks and live discussion, a Chenrezig practice is held on the first Thursday of each month, and people under thirty-five meet for a monthly one-day urban retreat. Longer retreats at Maitripa in November and at Easter combine shamatha meditation, Tara and Chenrezig practices and yoga, and can also be joined online. The Akshara bookshop sells Rinpoche's books, and several of his talk series are free to download.

courses.title: November Retreat 2026
courses.description: A four-day retreat at Maitripa Centre near Healesville and online, with shamatha meditation, Chenrezig and Green Tara practices, Indo-Tibetan yoga, guided meditation and recorded teachings by Traleg Kyabgon Rinpoche on the Four Immeasurables, plus study groups led by Traleg Khandro. Vegetarian meals included.

courses.title: Annual Easter Retreat
courses.description: The institute's yearly Easter retreat at Maitripa Centre and online, keeping Traleg Rinpoche's retreat format: sitting and walking meditation, morning and evening Tara and Chenrezig practices, yoga and his recorded teachings. Partial attendance is possible.

courses.title: Associate Membership
courses.description: Entry-level membership with a discount on courses and the bookshop, the quarterly Meditation and Teachings series, support for beginning the Ngondro preliminary practices and guidance on solo retreats; members are asked to help at working bees.
courses.price: Annual fee for Associate Membership is $269 for single membership and $405 for family membership

free_resources.title: A Series of Four Talks on the Four Brahmaviharas
free_resources.description: Four talks by Traleg Kyabgon Rinpoche, free as a PDF, on cultivating the four boundless qualities of love, compassion, joy and equanimity, on the cushion and in everyday life.

free_resources.title: Religion and Spirituality
free_resources.description: Three talks by Traleg Kyabgon Rinpoche, free as a PDF, on whether Buddhism should be called a religion, a spiritual path or both, and the many meanings of each word.
